# PART I: Foundations of LBBNN & Input-Skip Architecture (ISLaB)

## Motivation — What Official Statistics Truly Requires

\vspace{-0.15em}
\textbf{The Primary Mandate of Official Statistics:}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Unbiased Finite Population \& Domain Inference}: Calibrated, design-consistent estimation of finite-population parameters (means, totals, sub-domain distributions) with valid uncertainty quantification.
  \item \textbf{Dual Transparency (Global \& Local)}: Structural feature selection at the population level (global sparsity) and verifiable respondent-level sensitivity attributions (local polyhedral GLMs).
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

\vspace{0.15em}
\textbf{The Reality of Complex Modern Data Regimes:}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Non-Linear Participation Bias}: In opt-in and administrative sources ($S_c$), self-selection mechanisms are non-linear functions of respondent covariates—standard linear logit models are structurally misspecified.
  \item \textbf{Differential Stratification \& Informative Designs}: Sample inclusion probabilities differ across demographic strata, requiring \textbf{pseudo-posterior likelihood reweighting} to correct selection bias.
  \item \textbf{Formal Differential Privacy ($\epsilon, \delta$)}: Skewed economic microdata (wages, firm revenues) contain extreme leverage records that threaten re-identification, requiring privacy calibration that preserves distributional shape.
  \item \textbf{Weight-Variance Protection}: Dense deep models retain pure noise covariates, triggering severe variance inflation in downstream Horvitz–Thompson and H\'{a}jek weighting.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

## From Dense BNNs to Latent Binary BNNs (Hubin & Storvik, 2024)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Spike-and-Slab Edge Selection:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Latent binary inclusion indicator $\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)} \in \{0, 1\}$:
  \small
  $$p\big(w_{k,p}^{(j)} \mid \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\mathcal{N}\big(0, (\tau_{k,p}^{(j)})^2\big) + \big(1-\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)\delta_0$$
  $$p\big(\gamma_{k,p}^{(j)}\big) = \text{Bernoulli}\big(\psi_{k,p}^{(j)}\big)$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA)}: Ensembles across posterior draws $\Gamma \sim q(\Gamma)$ and $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma)$ for optimal uncertainty quantification.
  \item \textbf{Median Probability Model (MPM)}: Hard-prunes edges with posterior inclusion probability $a_{k,p}^{(j)} \le 0.5$ (Barbieri \& Berger, 2004 optimal predictive submodel).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Input-Skip LBBNNs (ISLaB) & Structural Depth Metrics (Høyheim et al., 2026)

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{The ISLaB Architecture (\textit{JAIR}, 2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Direct skips route inputs $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ to every hidden layer: $\mathbf{a}^{(j-1)} = [a_1^{(j-1)}, \dots, a_K^{(j-1)}, \mathbf{x}^\top]^\top$.
  \item \textbf{Active Path ($\text{AP}$)}: Connects input $x_k$ to output $\zeta$ via edges with $a_{k,p}^{(j)} > 0.5$.
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Contribution Depth Classification:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Depth = 1}: Direct skip $\implies$ linear GLM effect.
  \item \textbf{Depth $\ge$ 2}: Hidden layers $\implies$ non-linear interaction.
  \item \textbf{Paths = 0}: Noise covariate pruned from graph.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}

## Local Explainability via Polyhedral ReLU Activation Regions

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Local GLM Theorem (JSM 2026):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Piecewise-linear activations partition $\mathbb{R}^p$ into polyhedral activation regions $\mathcal{P}_1, \dots, \mathcal{P}_M$.
  \item Within each local region $\mathcal{P}_m$, the active network reduces to an exact \textbf{local GLM}:
  \small
  $$\zeta(\mathbf{x}) = \beta_0(\mathbf{x}_i) + \sum_{j=1}^p \beta_j(\mathbf{x}_i) x_j$$
  $$\boldsymbol{\beta}(\mathbf{x}_i) = \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \zeta(\mathbf{x})\big|_{\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{x}_i}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Exact Gradients}: Evaluated via analytical backpropagation (zero perturbation error).
  \item \textbf{Credible Intervals}: Draws $W \sim q(W \mid \Gamma^*)$ yield exact posterior intervals for respondent sensitivities.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/jsm_polyhedral_regions.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Variational Inference & Protection Against Cold Posteriors

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Variational ELBO at True $T = 1.0$:}
\small
$$\text{ELBO}(q) = \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}_{q}[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)] - \text{KL}(q \parallel p)$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Why Explicit Error Scale $\sigma^2$ Matters (Wenzel et al., 2020):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Omitting residual noise scale $\sigma^2$ artificially rescales likelihood ($T = \sigma^2 \neq 1$), mis-calibrating spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
  \item In \texttt{lbbnn\_net(sigma = ...)}, calibrated $\sigma^2$ grounds log-likelihood sensitivities on the true Bayesian scale.
  \item Calibrates both feature inclusion probabilities $a_k$ and DP sensitivities $f_i$.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/jsm_variational_elbo.pdf}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

# PART II: Track 1 — Unit-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors & Formal Differential Privacy

## Unit-Weighted Variational Pseudo-Posteriors (Savitsky & Toth, 2016)

\vspace{0.2em}
Equipping each unit $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$ with a non-negative weight $u_i \ge 0$ defines the pseudo-posterior:
\small
$$p_{\mathbf{u}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}) \propto p(\theta) \prod_{i=1}^n f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)^{u_i}$$
$$\text{ELBO}(q; \mathbf{u}) = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \, \mathbb{E}_{q(\theta)}\!\left[\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)\right] - \text{KL}\big(q(\theta) \parallel p(\theta)\big)$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.5em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{1. Survey Sampling Weights ($u_i = \tilde{w}_i$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Normalized to sample size $n$: $\tilde{w}_i = w_i \frac{n}{\sum w_j}$.
  \item Setting \texttt{normalize\_weights = TRUE} ensures $\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$ does not overpower spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
  \item Corrects informative sampling selection bias.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{2. Differential Privacy Weights ($u_i = \alpha_i$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Unnormalized weights: $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$.
  \item Setting \texttt{normalize\_weights = FALSE} ensures $\sum \alpha_i \le n$.
  \item Downweights high-sensitivity tail outliers and contracts the pseudo-posterior toward the prior.
\end{itemize}
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Track 1A — Informative Survey Sampling Setup & Automated Noise Pruning

\vspace{0.1em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
\textbf{Simulation Setup ($N = 2,000, p = 4$):}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{True Non-Linear DGP}:
  \small
  $$Y_i = 2 X_{1i} + 1.5 \sin(\pi X_{2i}) + 0.8 X_{1i} X_{2i} + \varepsilon_i$$
  \normalsize
  where $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 0.4^2)$, and $X_3, X_4 \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ are pure noise.
  \item \textbf{Informative Selection Mechanism}:
  \small
  $$\pi_i = \sigma(-1.0 + 1.2 Y_i), \qquad \sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}$$
  \normalsize
  Draws $n = 737$ units favoring high $Y_i$.
  \item Unweighted sample mean is \textbf{+2.009} (True population mean: \textbf{0.000}).
\end{itemize}
\end{column}

## Track 1A — Domain Estimation, Imputation & Dirichlet Bootstrap UQ

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Domain Totals \& Conditional Expectations:}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Domain Membership Matrix} $\mathbf{G} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times D_{\text{dom}}}$ defines sub-populations:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{\text{BNN}(s)} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i G_{i,d} \, \hat{\mu}_i^{(s)}}{\sum_{i=1}^n w_i G_{i,d}}$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item \textbf{Model-Assisted Conditional Mean}: Evaluating $\hat{\mu}_i^{(s)} = \mathbb{E}[Y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta^{(s)}]$ (\texttt{type = "conditional\_mean"}) estimates the smooth regression surface without adding simulation noise $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$.
  \item \textbf{Item Non-Response Imputation}: Missing outcomes ($y_i = \text{NA}$) are filled via full posterior predictive draws $\tilde{y}_i^{(s)} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{\theta^{(s)}}(\mathbf{x}_i), \sigma^2)$ (\texttt{impute\_response\_lbbnn}).
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Dirichlet Bayesian Bootstrap UQ:}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Pseudo-Posterior Variance Deficit}: Conditioning on fixed sample $S$ captures parameter uncertainty $\theta^{(s)} \sim q(\theta)$ but underestimates design-based sampling variance.
  \item \textbf{Joint Parameter + Design Perturbations} (Savitsky \& Toth, 2016): For each posterior draw $s \in \{1, \dots, S\}$, sample $\theta^{(s)} \sim q(\theta)$ \emph{and} flat weights $\boldsymbol{\xi}^{(s)} \sim \text{Dirichlet}(1, \dots, 1)$:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{(s)} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i^{(s)} w_i G_{i,d} \, \hat{\mu}_i^{(s)}}{\sum_{i=1}^n \xi_i^{(s)} w_i G_{i,d}}$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item Compounds epistemic BNN uncertainty with survey design variability (\texttt{dirichlet\_uq = TRUE}).
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Pipeline & Return Structures: Survey-Weighted LBBNN (Track 1A)

\vspace{-0.3em}
\scriptsize
```r
# 1. Package design weights & allow missing response values (y_i = NA)
dl_train <- get_dataloaders(df_survey, weights = w_design, normalize_weights = TRUE,
                            allow_missing = TRUE, train_batch_size = 64, test_batch_size = 32)
# 2. Build LBBNN with calibrated residual noise scale sigma (protects T=1)
net <- lbbnn_net(problem_type = "regression", sizes = c(p, 16, 1),
                 sigma = 0.4, input_skip = TRUE)
fit <- train_lbbnn(LBBNN = net, train_dl = dl_train$train_loader, epochs = 100, lr = 0.01)
# 3. Domain predictions & Bayesian imputation with Dirichlet uncertainty draws
dom_est <- predict_domains_lbbnn(net, X, domain_matrix = G, weights = w_design,
                                 type = "conditional_mean", dirichlet_uq = TRUE, draws = 50)
imp_res <- impute_response_lbbnn(net, newdata = df_survey, target_col = "y", draws = 50)
```
\normalsize

## Track 1B — Why Unweighted Neural Networks Fail Differential Privacy

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{Probabilistic Differential Privacy (Savitsky, Williams \& Hu, 2022):}
\small
$$\sup_{\theta \in \Theta_\delta} \left|\log \frac{q_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y})}{q_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}(\theta \mid \mathbf{y}')}\right| \le \epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 2 \Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}}, \qquad \Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = \max_{s, i} |\alpha_i \log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta^{(s)})|$$
\normalsize

\vspace{0.4em}
\textbf{The Quadratic Exposure Dilemma in Gaussian Regression:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Pointwise Gaussian log-likelihood grows quadratically with the residual:
  $$|\log f(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \theta)| \propto \frac{(y_i - \mu_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i))^2}{2\sigma^2}$$
  \item In skewed survey microdata (wages, financial expenditures), extreme outliers drive unweighted sensitivity $\Delta \to \infty$ and privacy budget $\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} \to \infty$.
  \item Naive gradient clipping distorts the mean and destroys the variance structure of official statistics.
\end{itemize}

## Track 1B — Multi-Pass Privacy Calibration Pipeline (`fit_dp_lbbnn`)

\vspace{-0.1em}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.71, every node/.style={scale=0.71, font=\sffamily}]
  \node[rectangle, draw=blue!80, fill=blue!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.3cm, align=center] (p1) at (0, 0) {\textbf{Pass 1}\\[2pt]Unweighted Fit\\[2pt]($u_i = 1$, $\hat{\sigma}$)};

  \node[rectangle, draw=purple!80, fill=purple!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.7cm, align=center] (weight) at (7.2, 0) {\textbf{2-Stage Weights}\\[2pt]Stage 1: $\alpha_i^{(1)} \in [0,1]$\\[2pt]Stage 2: $\alpha_i^* f_i \le M_{\text{thresh}}$};
  \node[rectangle, draw=green!70!black, fill=green!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.5cm, align=center] (p2) at (10.8, 0) {\textbf{Pass 2 / Pass 3}\\[2pt]$\alpha^*$-Weighted Fit\\[2pt]$\Delta_{\alpha,\mathbf{y}} \le M_{\text{thresh}}$};
  \node[rectangle, draw=red!80, fill=red!10, rounded corners, thick, text width=2.2cm, align=center] (synth) at (14.2, 0) {\textbf{Synthesis}\\[2pt]$(\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}}, \delta)$-PDP Microdata};
  
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (p1) -- (risk);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (risk) -- (weight);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (weight) -- (p2);
  \draw[->, thick, >=stealth] (p2) -- (synth);
\end{tikzpicture}

\vspace{0.15em}
\footnotesize
\textbf{Definitions \& End-to-End Privacy Verification:}
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Pass 1 Pointwise Log-Likelihood ($L_{s,i}^{(1)}$)}: Evaluated across $s = 1, \dots, S$ unweighted posterior draws $\theta^{(1,s)} \sim q^{(1)}(\theta)$ to measure worst-case record sensitivity $f_i = \max_{s} |L_{s,i}^{(1)}|$.
  \item \textbf{Two-Stage Weight Calibration ($\alpha_i^{(1)} \to \alpha_i^*$)}: Stage 1 maps $f_i$ to an initial weight $\alpha_i^{(1)} \in [0, 1]$; Stage 2 enforces the sensitivity threshold $\alpha_i^* f_i \le M_{\text{thresh}}$.
  \item \textbf{Empirical Lipschitz Bound}: After fitting the $\alpha^*$-weighted pseudo-posterior (Pass 2, plus Pass 3 if vector rescaling shifts geometry), verify $\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} = \max_{s,i} |\alpha_i^* L_{s,i}^{(\text{final})}| \le M_{\text{thresh}}$, guaranteeing $\epsilon_{\mathbf{y}} = 2\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}}$.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

## Track 1B — Stage 1: Initial Privacy Weight Normalization on $f_i$ (Savitsky, 2026)

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.51\textwidth}
\textbf{Direct Normalization of $f_i = \max_s |L_{s,i}^{(1)}|$ into $\alpha_i^{(1)}$:}
\footnotesize
\begin{enumerate}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Linear Min-Max on $f_i$} (\texttt{"linear"}):
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\tilde{f}_i = \frac{f_i - f_{\min}}{f_{\max} - f_{\min}}, \quad \alpha_i^{\text{lin}} = c(1 - \tilde{f}_i) = c\frac{f_{\max} - f_i}{f_{\max} - f_{\min}}$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item \textbf{Percentile Deficit Truncation} (\texttt{"percentile"}):
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{pct}} = \min\!\left(1, \, \max\!\left(0, \, \frac{q_{p_R}(f) - f_i}{q_{p_R}(f) - q_{p_L}(f)}\right)\right)$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item \textbf{Target Ratio Clipping} (\texttt{"target\_clip"}):
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{clip}} = \min\!\left(1, \, \frac{\Delta_{i, \text{goal}}}{f_i}\right)$$
\end{enumerate}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.49\textwidth}
\textbf{Key Theoretical Insights (Savitsky, 2026):}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Direct $1 - \tilde{f}_i$ vs. Reciprocal $1/f_i$ (Remark 1)}: Normalizing $1/f_i$ induces hyperbolic attenuation $\alpha_i^{\text{recip}} = (f_{\min}/f_i)\alpha_i^{\text{lin}}$, collapsing weights when $f_{\min} \to 0$. Direct $1 - \tilde{f}_i$ prevents collapse; $\alpha_i^{\text{lin}}f_i$ peaks at $f_{\max}/2$ ($\le \frac{c}{4}f_{\max}$).
  \item \textbf{Percentile Boosting}: Sets $\alpha_i^{\text{pct}} = 1$ for $f_i \le q_{p_L}(f)$ and $0$ for $f_i \ge q_{p_R}(f)$, boosting $\sum \alpha_i^{(1)}$ while Stage 2 caps $\alpha_i^* f_i$.
  \item \textbf{Exact Target Control (Prop. 1)}: $\alpha_i^{\text{clip}} f_i \le \Delta_{\text{goal}}$ by construction; all moderate units ($f_i \le \Delta_{\text{goal}}$) retain full weight $\alpha_i^{(1)} = 1$.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Track 1B — Stage 2: Enforcing the Threshold ($\alpha_i^* f_i \le M_{\text{thresh}}$)

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{Second-Stage Reweighting Schemes ($\alpha_i^{(1)} \to \alpha_i^*$):}
\footnotesize
\begin{enumerate}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{4pt}
  \item \textbf{Hard Truncation (\texttt{"hard\_trunc"})}:
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{trunc}} = \alpha_i^{(1)} \, \mathbb{I}\!\left(\alpha_i^{(1)} f_i \le M_{\text{thresh}}\right)$$
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  Post-hoc zeroing of records where $\alpha_i^{(1)} f_i > M_{\text{thresh}}$; leaves unspent privacy capacity $M_{\text{thresh}} - \alpha_i^{(1)} f_i > 0$ on surviving units.
  \item \textbf{Vector Upward Rescaling (\texttt{"vector\_upscale"})}:
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  $$\alpha_i^{\text{vec}} = \min\!\left(1, \, \alpha_i^{(1)} \cdot \frac{M_{\text{thresh}}}{\alpha_i^{(1)} f_i}\right) = \min\!\left(1, \, \frac{M_{\text{thresh}}}{f_i}\right)$$
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  Inflates all active weights ($\alpha_i^{(1)} > 0$) up to the privacy threshold boundary; pointwise dominates hard truncation ($\alpha_i^{\text{vec}} \ge \alpha_i^{\text{trunc}}$).
\end{enumerate}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{Information Dominance \& Multi-Pass Geometry:}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Algebraic Cancellation Insight}: For any record with $\alpha_i^{(1)} > 0$, $\alpha_i^{(1)}$ cancels in $\alpha_i^{\text{vec}}$, collapsing directly to $\min(1, M_{\text{thresh}}/f_i)$ (\texttt{target\_clip}). If Stage 1 zeroes tail units (\texttt{percentile}), those zeroes remain preserved.
  \item \textbf{Loewner Fisher Dominance (Prop. 2)}: Because $\alpha_i^{\text{vec}} \ge \alpha_i^{\text{trunc}}$ everywhere, vector upward rescaling strictly maximizes Fisher information:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\mathcal{I}_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{\text{vec}}}(\theta) \succeq \mathcal{I}_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{\text{trunc}}}(\theta)$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item \textbf{Why Pass 3 Is Executed}: Upward rescaling shifts the pseudo-posterior geometry $\xi_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}^{\text{vec}}}(\theta \mid D)$; \texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn()} executes Pass 3 on $\alpha_i^{\text{vec}}$ to verify $\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} \le M_{\text{thresh}}$ on the final variational draws.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

# PART III: Track 2 — Combining Probability & Non-Probability Samples

## The Big Data Paradox in Convenience Samples (Meng, 2018)

\vspace{0.2em}
\textbf{The Non-Probability Selection Dilemma:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Let $U = \{1, \dots, N\}$ denote the finite target population of size $N$.
  \item In convenience/opt-in samples $S_c \subset U$, sample inclusion $I_{ci} \in \{0, 1\}$ is non-random and driven by unobserved self-selection mechanisms.
  \item \textbf{Meng's Law of Large Populations (2018)}:
  \small
  $$\text{Bias}(\bar{y}_c) = \frac{\text{Cov}_U(I_c, Y)}{\bar{\pi}_c} = \rho_{I_c, Y} \cdot \sigma_Y \cdot \sqrt{\frac{N - n_c}{n_c}}$$
  \normalsize
  \item \textbf{Exact Definitions}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $\pi_{ci} = \mathbb{P}(I_{ci} = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i)$: Unknown propensity that unit $i$ with covariates $\mathbf{x}_i$ self-selects into $S_c$.
    \item $\bar{\pi}_c = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i \in U} \pi_{ci}$: Average participation propensity across the entire target population $U$.
  \end{itemize}
  \item A tiny correlation $\rho_{I_c, Y} \neq 0$ creates selection bias scaling with $\sqrt{N}$; increasing sample size $n_c$ merely concentrates error around a severely biased estimate.
\end{itemize}

## The Identification Barrier & The Conditioning Principle (Beresovsky et al., 2026)

\vspace{-0.15em}
\textbf{The Missing Mass \& Identification Barrier:}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item Let $U = \{1, \dots, N\}$ denote the finite target population. We observe covariates $\mathbf{x}_i \in \mathbb{R}^p$ on two samples:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \footnotesize
    \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
    \item \textbf{Convenience Sample $S_c$ ($n_c$ units)}: Self-selected with \emph{unknown} propensity $\pi_{ci} = \mathbb{P}(I_{ci} = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i) = \sigma(\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i))$, where $\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}$, and observed survey outcome $y_i$.
    \item \textbf{Reference Probability Survey $S_r$ ($n_r$ units)}: Selected with \emph{known} design inclusion probability $\pi_{ri} = \mathbb{P}(I_{ri} = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i) > 0$, measuring shared covariates $\mathbf{x}_i$ (outcomes $y_i$ unobserved).
  \end{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Why Direct Binary Classification Fails}: Fitting a direct Bernoulli likelihood for $I_{ci} \in \{0, 1\}$ across $U$ is impossible because non-sampled population units $i \in U \setminus (S_c \cup S_r)$ are completely unobserved.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

\vspace{0.15em}
\textbf{The Conditioning Resolution (Quasi-Randomization vs. Pseudo-Likelihood):}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Composite Conditioning}: Pool $S_c$ and $S_r$ into a combined sample $S$, and condition on inclusion $i \in S$. Known design probabilities $\pi_{ri}$ enter $\pi_{zi} = \mathbb{P}(I_{zi} = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i, i \in S)$ as a structural anchor, rendering $\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)$ fully identifiable!
  \item \textbf{Survey Design Pseudo-Likelihood (\texttt{PSEUDO})}: Approximate the unobserved population log-likelihood over $U$ using Horvitz–Thompson inverse design weights $w_{ri} = \pi_{ri}^{-1}$ on $S_r$ (Chen, Li \& Wu, 2020).
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

## Intuition & Torch Training Link for All Five Estimators

\vspace{-0.2em}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.18}
\scriptsize
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{p{0.12\textwidth}p{0.21\textwidth}p{0.21\textwidth}p{0.41\textwidth}}
\toprule
\textbf{Estimator} & \textbf{Sample Overlap} & \textbf{Composite Prob $\pi_{zi}$} & \textbf{Torch Backprop \& Loss Link} \\
\midrule
\texttt{STACK} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Unlinked) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ & Offset $\text{logit}(\pi_{zi}) = \eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i) - \log \pi_{ri}$ in Bernoulli NLL. \\
\texttt{LINK1} & $S_c \cup (S_r \setminus S_c)$ & $\frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri} - \pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}}$ & Deduplicated union; backprops through $-\pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}$ overlap adjustment. \\
\texttt{LINK2} & $S_c \oplus S_r$ (Linked Stack) & $\frac{\pi_{ci}(1 + \pi_{ri})}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$ & Exact indicator $I_{zi} = D_i + (1-D_i)I_{ci}$; maximizes Fisher information. \\
\texttt{MIP} & Missing Information & Bridges \texttt{STACK} \& \texttt{LINK2} & Evaluates expectation $\tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}} = D_i + (1-D_i)\tilde{p}_i$ with $\tilde{p}_i \in [0, 1]$. \\
\texttt{PSEUDO} & Survey-Weighted & Design pseudo-likelihood & Score: $\sum_{S_r} \pi_{ri}^{-1}\text{softplus}(\eta_i) +$ \newline $\sum_{S_c} \log(1 + e^{-\eta_i}) = 0$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\normalsize

\vspace{-0.4em}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
  \item \textbf{Composite vs. Pseudo}: Composite likelihoods (\texttt{STACK}, \texttt{LINK1}, \texttt{LINK2}, \texttt{MIP}) form relative odds fractions that naturally bound loss gradients, whereas \texttt{PSEUDO} multiplies unconstrained logits by $\pi_{ri}^{-1}$.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

## Implementation in `LBBNN` (1/5): `STACK` (Unlinked Stacked Sample)

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{Statistical Formulation ($S = S_c \oplus S_r$):}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Unlinked Multiset}: Pool $S_c$ ($n_c$) and $S_r$ ($n_r$) into a multiset of size $n = n_c + n_r$ with origin indicator $I_{zi} = D_i = \mathbb{I}(i \in S_c) \in \{0, 1\}$:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\pi_{zi}^{\text{STACK}} = \frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}, \qquad \pi_{ci} = \sigma\big(\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)\big) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)}}$$
  \vspace{-0.25em}
  \item \textbf{Log-Odds \& Rare-Event Offset ($\pi_{ci} \ll 1$)}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \log\!\left(\frac{\pi_{zi}^{\text{STACK}}}{1 - \pi_{zi}^{\text{STACK}}}\right) &= \log \pi_{ci} - \log \pi_{ri} \\
  &= \eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i) - \underbrace{\log\big(1 + e^{\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)}\big)}_{\approx 0 \text{ when } \pi_{ci} \ll 1} - \log \pi_{ri}
  \end{aligned}$$
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  When $\pi_{ci} \ll 1$ ($n_c \ll N$), $-\log \pi_{ri}$ acts as an additive offset.
  \item \textbf{Exact Composite NLL}: In \texttt{nll\_stack()}, we evaluate the exact fraction $\frac{\sigma(\eta_i)}{\sigma(\eta_i) + \pi_{ri}}$ without dropping $\log(1 + e^{\eta_i})$, guaranteeing exact calibration at any sampling fraction.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{LibTorch Architecture (\texttt{nll\_stack}):}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Dataset Packaging}: \texttt{build\_propensity\_dataset(pop, method = "STACK")} binds covariates $\mathbf{X}$ with target tensor $\mathbf{Y} = [D_i, \pi_{ri}] \in \mathbb{R}^{(n_c + n_r) \times 2}$.
  \item \textbf{Bernoulli Composite Loss}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{STACK}}(\theta) &= -\sum_{i \in S_c \oplus S_r} \Big[ D_i \log \hat{\pi}_{zi}^{\text{STACK}} \\
  &\quad + (1 - D_i)\log\big(1 - \hat{\pi}_{zi}^{\text{STACK}}\big) \Big]
  \end{aligned}$$
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  \item \textbf{Bounded Gradients}: Because $\pi_{ri} > 0$ sits inside the denominator $\hat{\pi}_{ci} + \pi_{ri}$, loss gradients with respect to $\eta_i$ are strictly bounded in $[-1, 1]$ even when $\pi_{ri} \to 0$.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Implementation in `LBBNN` (2/5): `LINK1` (Deterministically Linked Union)

\vspace{-0.15em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{Statistical Formulation ($S = S_c \cup (S_r \setminus S_c)$):}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Deduplicated Union Sample}: Exact identifiers match overlapping units $S_c \cap S_r$, which are dropped from the reference block, leaving $n = n_c + n_r - |S_c \cap S_r|$ unique units.
  \item \textbf{Target Indicator}: $I_{zi} = I_{ci} \in \{0, 1\}$ ($1$ if unit $i \in S_c$, $0$ if $i \in S_r \setminus S_c$).
  \item \textbf{Conditional Independence Overlap}: Under $\mathbb{P}(I_{ci}=1, I_{ri}=1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i) = \pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}$, inclusion in the union is $\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri} - \pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}$:
  $$\pi_{zi}^{\text{LINK1}} = \frac{\pi_{ci}}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri} - \pi_{ci}\pi_{ri}}$$
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{LibTorch Architecture (\texttt{nll\_link1}):}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Dataset Packaging}: \texttt{build\_propensity\_dataset(pop, method = "LINK1")} filters out reference records with $I_{ci} = 1$ and constructs $\mathbf{Y} = [I_{zi}, \pi_{ri}]$.
  \item \textbf{Overlap-Adjusted Backprop}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \scriptsize
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{LINK1}}(\theta) &= -\sum_{i \in S_{\text{union}}} \Big[ I_{zi} \log \pi_{zi}^{\text{LINK1}} \\
  &\quad + (1 - I_{zi})\log(1 - \pi_{zi}^{\text{LINK1}}) \Big]
  \end{aligned}$$
  \footnotesize
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item Autograd differentiates directly through the non-linear product $-\hat{\pi}_{ci}\pi_{ri}$ in the denominator, correcting for the removal of duplicate units.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Implementation in `LBBNN` (3/5): `LINK2` (Deterministically Linked Stack)

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.53\textwidth}
\textbf{Deterministic Linking on Stacked Multiset ($S_c \oplus S_r$):}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Multiset Retention ($n = n_c + n_r$)}: Unlike \texttt{LINK1} (which drops duplicates), \texttt{LINK2} retains all stacked records—units in $S_c \cap S_r$ physically appear twice (once in $S_c$ with $D_i=1$, once in $S_r$ with $D_i=0$).
  \item \textbf{Deterministic Re-Labeling via Unique IDs}: Exact identifiers reveal $I_{ci} = \mathbb{I}(i \in S_c) \in \{0, 1\}$ for every unit in $S_r$. We define the composite indicator:
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  $$I_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}} = D_i + (1 - D_i)I_{ci} \in \{0, 1\}$$
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  Both copies of overlapping units ($D_i=1$ and matched $D_i=0, I_{ci}=1$) receive label $I_{zi}=1$; only confirmed non-participants ($D_i=0, I_{ci}=0$) receive $I_{zi}=0$.
  \item \textbf{Expected Instance Ratio}: Expected count of $I_{zi}=1$ instances is $\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}\pi_{ci} = \pi_{ci}(1+\pi_{ri})$ out of $\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}$ total instances:
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  $$\pi_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}} = \frac{\pi_{ci}(1 + \pi_{ri})}{\pi_{ci} + \pi_{ri}}$$
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.47\textwidth}
\textbf{LibTorch Architecture (\texttt{nll\_link2}):}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Dataset Packaging}: \texttt{build\_propensity\_dataset(pop, method = "LINK2")} packs $\mathbf{Y} = [I_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}}, \pi_{ri}] \in \mathbb{R}^{(n_c + n_r) \times 2}$.
  \item \textbf{Loss Closure}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \scriptsize
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{LINK2}}(\theta) &= -\sum_{i \in S_c \oplus S_r} \bigg[ I_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}} \log\!\left(\frac{\hat{\pi}_{ci}(1+\pi_{ri})}{\hat{\pi}_{ci}+\pi_{ri}}\right) \\
  &\quad + (1-I_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}})\log\!\left(\frac{\pi_{ri}(1-\hat{\pi}_{ci})}{\hat{\pi}_{ci}+\pi_{ri}}\right) \bigg]
  \end{aligned}$$
  \footnotesize
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item \textbf{Fisher Information Optimality}: Resolves label ambiguity on overlapping records in $S_r$, strictly maximizing Fisher information across all composite estimators.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Implementation in `LBBNN` (4/5): `MIP` (Missing Information Principle)

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{Probabilistic Record Linkage Origin:}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Latent Overlap ($I_{ci}$ Missing on $S_r$)}: When noisy quasi-identifiers or privacy rules preclude deterministic linking, an upstream linkage model (e.g., Fellegi–Sunter) estimates pairwise match probabilities $m_{ij} = \mathbb{P}(i \sim j \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j)$, yielding marginal reference linkage scores:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\tilde{p}_i = \sum_{j \in S_c} m_{ij} \in [0, 1], \qquad \tilde{\mathbf{p}} = (\tilde{p}_1, \dots, \tilde{p}_{n_r})^\top$$
  \vspace{-0.25em}
  \item \textbf{EM Expectation Projection (Louis, 1982)}: Replace latent $I_{ci}$ in $I_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}}$ with its conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}[I_{ci} \mid \text{linkage}] = \tilde{p}_i$:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}} = D_i + (1 - D_i)\tilde{p}_i \in [0, 1]$$
  \vspace{-0.25em}
  \item \textbf{Benchmark DGPs vs. Production}: In production, $\tilde{\mathbf{p}}$ is supplied upstream by agency linkage software. In Studies 0–3, we simulate $\tilde{p}_i = \sigma(\gamma_0 + \gamma_1 I_{ci} + e_i)$ across linkage sharpness regimes ($\gamma_1 \gg 0 \to \text{\texttt{LINK2}}$, $\gamma_1 = 0 \to \text{\texttt{STACK}}$).
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{LibTorch Architecture (\texttt{make\_nll\_mip}):}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{4-Column Target Tensor}: \texttt{build\_propensity\_dataset(..., method = "MIP", p\_link = p\_vec)} packs $\mathbf{Y} = [D_i, I_{ci}, \pi_{ri}, \tilde{p}_i] \in \mathbb{R}^{(n_c + n_r) \times 4}$.
  \item \textbf{Soft-Label Composite NLL}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{MIP}}(\theta) &= -\sum_{i \in S_c \oplus S_r} \Big[ \tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}} \log \pi_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}} \\
  &\quad + \big(1 - \tilde{I}_{zi}^{\text{MIP}}\big)\log(1 - \pi_{zi}^{\text{LINK2}}) \Big]
  \end{aligned}$$
  \vspace{-0.15em}
  \item \textbf{Record-by-Record Score Interpolation}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \scriptsize
    \item High-certainty matches ($\tilde{p}_i \approx 1$) pull gradients toward the high-efficiency \texttt{LINK2} score.
    \item Unmatched units ($\tilde{p}_i \approx 0$) safely revert toward the unlinked \texttt{STACK} score.
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Implementation in `LBBNN` (5/5): `PSEUDO` (Design-Weighted Pseudo-NLL)

\vspace{-0.25em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
\textbf{Census Approximation (Chen, Li \& Wu, 2020):}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
  \item \textbf{Step 1: Unobservable Population Target ($U$)}: Full population census Bernoulli log-likelihood over $U$:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\ell_U(\theta) = \sum_{i \in S_c} \log\!\left(\frac{\pi_{ci}}{1 - \pi_{ci}}\right) + \sum_{i \in U} \log(1 - \pi_{ci})$$
  \vspace{-0.25em}
  \item \textbf{Step 2: Horvitz–Thompson Substitution on $S_r$}: Approximate $\sum_{i \in U} \log(1 - \pi_{ci})$ via inverse design weights $w_{ri} = \pi_{ri}^{-1}$:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\ell_{\text{pseudo}}(\theta) = \sum_{i \in S_c} \log\!\left(\frac{\pi_{ci}}{1 - \pi_{ci}}\right) + \sum_{i \in S_r} \frac{1}{\pi_{ri}}\log(1 - \pi_{ci})$$
  \vspace{-0.25em}
  \item \textbf{Step 3: Exact Logit \& Softplus NLL}: Substituting $\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i) = \log\frac{\pi_{ci}}{1-\pi_{ci}}$ and $\log(1-\pi_{ci}) = -\text{softplus}(\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i))$:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\text{NLL}_{\text{pseudo}}(\theta) = -\sum_{i \in S_c} \eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i) + \sum_{i \in S_r} \frac{1}{\pi_{ri}}\,\text{softplus}\big(\eta_\theta(\mathbf{x}_i)\big)$$
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{LibTorch Architecture \& Low-Support Breakdown:}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Vectorized Closure (\texttt{nll\_pseudo})}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\begin{aligned}
  \mathcal{L}_{\text{PSEUDO}}(\theta) &= \sum_{i \in S_c \oplus S_r} \Big[ -D_i \eta_i \\
  &\quad + (1 - D_i)\pi_{ri}^{-1}\,\text{softplus}(\eta_i) \Big]
  \end{aligned}$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \item \textbf{Why \texttt{PSEUDO} Explodes Under Low Support}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\frac{\partial \text{NLL}_{\text{pseudo}}}{\partial \eta_i} = -D_i + (1 - D_i)\frac{\hat{\pi}_{ci}}{\pi_{ri}}$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \begin{itemize}
    \scriptsize
    \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
    \item Where convenience respondents prefer strata with $\pi_{ri} \to 0$, the multiplier $\hat{\pi}_{ci}/\pi_{ri} \to \infty$.
    \item Unlike composite likelihoods (gradients bounded in $[-1, 1]$), unbounded gradients destabilize variational updates and collapse Kish's ESS!
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Study 0 — Exact Linear Baseline Monte Carlo ($R = 20$, Beresovsky et al., 2026)

\vspace{-0.25em}
\scriptsize
\textbf{Data Generating Process ($N = 5,000, p = 3, R = 20$ Monte Carlo Replicates):}
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{0.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Covariates \& Outcome}: $(X_1, X_2, X_3)^\top \sim \mathcal{MVN}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$ ($\Sigma_{ii}=1, \Sigma_{12}=0.5, \Sigma_{13}=\Sigma_{23}=0.3$); $\quad Y_i = 1 + X_{1i} + X_{2i} + X_{3i} + \varepsilon_i$, $\varepsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1^2)$.
  \item \textbf{Sampling Designs ($n_r = 500, n_c \approx 500$)}: Reference PPS $\pi_{ri} \propto \sigma(X_{1i} + X_{2i})$; Convenience $\text{logit}(\pi_{ci}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} - 0.3 X_{2i}$ (\textbf{High Support}: $\beta_1 = +1.0$; \textbf{Low Support}: $\beta_1 = -1.0$).
\end{itemize}

\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.82\textwidth, height=0.36\textheight, keepaspectratio]{figures/track2_study0_rmse_bars.pdf}

\vspace{-0.25em}
\raggedright
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{0.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Oracle Benchmark \& Stein's Phenomenon}: In Panel B (Low Support), true propensities near $0$ create extreme $1/\pi_{ci}$ weights; \texttt{LBBNN} regularization smooths tail weights, achieving lower RMSE than the unregularized Oracle ($0.17$ vs. $0.224$).
  \item \textbf{Pseudo-Likelihood Breakdown}: Under low support, \texttt{GLM-PSEUDO} explodes to $\text{RMSE} = 1.015$, while composite formulations remain bounded ($\text{RMSE} \approx 0.14\text{--}0.33$).
\end{itemize}
\normalsize

## Study 1 — Automated Confounder Selection & Noise Pruning ($p = 6$)

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.49\textwidth}
\textbf{Data Generating Process ($N = 5,000, p = 6$):}
\scriptsize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
  \item \textbf{Covariates}: $(X_1, X_2, X_3) \sim \mathcal{MVN}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$ correlated; $X_4, X_5, X_6 \stackrel{\text{i.i.d.}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ pure noise.
  \item \textbf{Non-Linear Outcome ($Y_i$)}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \tiny
  $$Y_i = 1 + X_{1i} + X_{2i} + X_{3i} + 0.5X_{1i}^2 - 0.5\sin(\pi X_{2i}) + \varepsilon_i$$
  \scriptsize
  \item \textbf{Reference Survey ($S_r, n_r = 500$)}: Systematic PPS with $\pi_{ri} \propto \sigma(X_{1i} + X_{2i})$.
  \item \textbf{Convenience Sample ($S_c, n_c \approx 500$)}:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\text{logit}(\pi_{ci}) = \beta_0 + 1.0 X_{1i} - 0.5 X_{2i}$$
\end{itemize}

\vspace{0.05em}
\textbf{Why Variable Selection Matters (\texttt{LBBNN-STACK}):}
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
  \item $X_3$ drives $Y_i$ but not $I_{ci}$; forcing $X_3$ into $\hat{\pi}_{ci}$ inflates H\'{a}jek weight variance without reducing bias.
  \item \texttt{LBBNN-STACK} (shown right; consistent across \texttt{LINK1/2/MIP}) retains confounders $X_1, X_2$ ($a_k > 0.99$) and prunes $X_3\text{--}X_6$ ($a_k \le 0.038, \text{Paths}=0$).
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

## Pipeline & Return Structures: Composite Propensity (Track 2)

\vspace{-0.3em}
\scriptsize
```r
# 1. Format combined sample with vectorized linkage probabilities p_vec
prep    <- build_propensity_dataset(pop, method = "MIP",
                                    covar_cols = paste0("X", 1:p), p_link = p_vec_r)
dl_prop <- get_dataloaders(prep$data, target_cols = prep$target_cols,
                           train_batch_size = 64, test_batch_size = 32)
# 2. Fit LBBNN with composite Bernoulli loss anchored by pi_ri offset
net_prop <- lbbnn_net(problem_type = "custom", sizes = c(p, 8, 1),
                      raw_output = TRUE, nll = make_nll_mip())
train_lbbnn(LBBNN = net_prop, train_dl = dl_prop$train_loader, epochs = 150, lr = 0.02)
# 3. Predict convenience propensities pi_c_hat & compute debiased Hajek mean
logits_c    <- predict(net_prop, newdata = prep$data[prep$Sc_indices, 1:p], mpm = TRUE)
pi_c_hat    <- as.numeric(torch::torch_sigmoid(torch::torch_tensor(logits_c)))
y_bar_hajek <- hajek_estimate(y = pop$y[pop$I.c == 1], pi_hat = pi_c_hat, dirichlet_uq = TRUE)
```
\normalsize

## Discussion — Bridging Track 2 Propensity Weights with Track 1 Regression

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Two-Stage Quasi-Randomization (Track 2):}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Stage 1}: \texttt{LBBNN} propensity model estimates $\hat{\pi}_{ci} = \mathbb{P}(I_{ci} = 1 \mid \mathbf{x}_i)$.
  \item \textbf{Stage 2}: Apply outcome-agnostic H\'{a}jek weights:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\hat{w}_i = \hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1}, \qquad \hat{\bar{Y}}_{\text{Hajek}} = \frac{\sum_{i \in S_c} \hat{w}_i y_i}{\sum_{i \in S_c} \hat{w}_i}$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  to any survey response variable $y_i$.
  \item \textbf{Outcome-Only Sparsity}: Pruning $X_3$ (which predicts $Y$ but not $I_c$) prevents weight variance inflation.
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Doubly Robust Pseudo-Posterior Imputation:}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2pt}
  \item \textbf{Bridging Track 2 $\to$ Track 1}: Normalize inverse propensity weights to sample size:
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  $$\tilde{w}_i = \hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1} \frac{n_c}{\sum_{j \in S_c} \hat{\pi}_{cj}^{-1}}$$
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  and feed $u_i = \tilde{w}_i$ directly into a \textbf{Track 1 LBBNN regression model} for $y_i$.
  \item \textbf{Double Robustness}: Consistent if \emph{either} propensity model \emph{or} outcome regression is correctly specified.
  \item Outcome model retains $X_3$ via spike-and-slab, recovering optimal predictive accuracy!
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}

## Joint Estimation — Two-Head LBBNN for Propensity & Outcome

\vspace{-0.2em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
\textbf{End-to-End Joint Learning:}
\vspace{-0.3em}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
  \item \textbf{Shared Representation}: Covariates $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ pass through shared latent binary spike-and-slab layers $\mathbf{z}_{\text{shared}}$ with direct ISLaB skips.
  \item \textbf{Head 1 (Propensity $\hat{\pi}_{ci}$)}: Predicts $\hat{\pi}_{ci} = \sigma(\eta_\theta^{(\pi)}(\mathbf{x}_i))$ trained via composite likelihood ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{comp}}$: \texttt{MIP} or \texttt{STACK}).
  \item \textbf{Head 2 (Outcome $\hat{y}_i$)}: Predicts survey outcome $\hat{y}_i = \mu_\theta^{(y)}(\mathbf{x}_i, \hat{\pi}_{ci})$ using $\hat{\pi}_{ci}$ as a balancing control function, weighted by $\text{sg}(\hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1})$.
  \item \textbf{Joint Variational ELBO}:
  \vspace{-0.35em}
  \scriptsize
  $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal{L}_{\text{joint}}(q) &= \mathbb{E}_q\big[\mathcal{L}_{\text{comp}}(\hat{\pi}_c)\big] - \text{KL}\big(q(\theta) \parallel p(\theta)\big) \\ &\quad + \sum_{i \in S_c} \mathbb{E}_q\!\left[\text{sg}(\hat{\pi}_{ci}^{-1})\log p(y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i, \hat{\pi}_{ci})\right] \end{aligned}$$
  \footnotesize
  \vspace{-0.35em}
  \item \textbf{Unified Feature Attribution}: Confounders ($X_1, X_2$) are shared; outcome-only drivers ($X_3$) feed directly into Head 2 without inflating propensity variance!
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

# PART IV: Software Architecture, Key Takeaways & Synthesis

## Unified `LBBNN` Architecture Across Track 1 & Track 2

\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.05}
\tiny
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{p{3.8cm}p{2.4cm}p{7.2cm}}
\toprule
\textbf{Function / Module} & \textbf{Operational Track} & \textbf{Description \& Statistical Role} \\
\midrule
\texttt{get\_dataloaders()} & Track 1 \& 2 & Handles non-trainable weights $u_i \ge 0$, normalization, missing $y_i$, and multi-targets. \\
\texttt{lbbnn\_net(sigma, ...)} & Track 1 \& 2 & ELBO likelihood scaling by error variance $\sigma^2$ (cold-posterior protection). \\
\texttt{predict\_domains\_lbbnn()} & Track 1A (Surveys) & Vectorized domain means/totals, conditional expectation ($\hat{\mu}_i$), and Dirichlet UQ. \\
\texttt{impute\_response\_lbbnn()} & Track 1A (Surveys) & Bayesian multiple imputation for missing outcomes ($y_i = \text{NA}$) via posterior predictive draws. \\
\texttt{compute\_dp\_weights()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Modular Stage 1 (\texttt{linear}, \texttt{percentile}, \texttt{target\_clip}) $\times$ Stage 2 (\texttt{hard\_trunc}, \texttt{vector\_upscale}). \\
\texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Multi-pass $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PDP estimation; executes Pass 3 under vector upward rescaling. \\
\texttt{sample\_synthetic\_lbbnn()} & Track 1B (Privacy) & Generates $(\epsilon, \delta)$-DP synthetic microdata via the post-processing theorem. \\
\midrule
\texttt{make\_nll\_mip(p\_link)} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Missing Information Principle NLL supporting scalar or vectorized unit-level linkage $\tilde{\mathbf{p}}$. \\
\texttt{nll\_link1()} / \texttt{nll\_link2()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Composite Bernoulli NLL on singly matched and matched-pair samples. \\
\texttt{nll\_stack()} / \texttt{nll\_pseudo()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Stacked pooled sample NLL and survey design-weighted pseudo-NLL. \\
\texttt{build\_propensity\_dataset()} & Track 2 (Propensity) & Formats covariates and targets for any of the 5 estimation methods. \\
\texttt{hajek\_estimate()} & Track 1 \& 2 & Self-normalizing H\'{a}jek mean with optional domain matrix $\mathbf{G}$ and Dirichlet bootstrap UQ. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
\normalsize

## Key Takeaways & Synthesis for Official Statistics

\vspace{0.2em}
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Survey-Weighted Pseudo-Posteriors (Track 1A)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Normalizing survey weights to sample size ($\sum \tilde{w}_i = n$) + calibrated observation noise $\sigma^2$ prevents likelihood mis-scaling ($T \neq 1$) and protects spike-and-slab KL shrinkage.
      \item \texttt{LBBNN} achieves 5x lower population RMSE than classical H\'{a}jek weighting under informative sampling while pruning irrelevant covariates.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Multi-Pass $(\epsilon, \delta)$-PDP Microdata Synthesis (Track 1B)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Full $3 \times 2$ factorial evaluation confirms Savitsky's (2026) theory: Stage 1 direct normalization ($1 - \tilde{f}_i$, \texttt{percentile}, \texttt{target\_clip}) avoids the severe ESS collapse of reciprocal $1/f_i$ weighting (Remark 1).
      \item Stage 2 vector upward rescaling (\texttt{vector\_upscale}) Loewner-dominates hard truncation (Prop. 2), retaining full weight ($\alpha_i^* = 1$) on safe inliers ($\text{ESS} = 285.5/300$) while strictly capping sensitivity at $\Delta_{\alpha, \mathbf{y}} \le M_{\text{thresh}}$ after Pass 3 retraining.
    \end{itemize}
  \vspace{0.3em}
  \item \textbf{Composite Non-Probability Sample Integration (Track 2)}:
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Conditioning on pooled sample inclusion $S_c \cup S_r$ allows known design probabilities $\pi_{ri}$ to anchor neural network logits to the true population scale.
      \item Composite Bernoulli likelihoods (\texttt{LINK2}, \texttt{LINK1}, \texttt{MIP}, \texttt{STACK}) bound loss gradients and prevent the catastrophic effective sample size collapse (\texttt{Kish ESS} $< 7$) of pseudo-likelihood under low common support.
    \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}

## Strategic Discussion — CRAN Packaging & Ecosystem Roadmap

\vspace{0.1em}
\textbf{Architectural Question: Where Should the Official Statistics \& DP Modules Live?}

\vspace{0.3em}
\begin{columns}
\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Option A: Monolithic Integration (\texttt{LBBNN} on CRAN)}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Single Unified Package}: Ship unit-weighted pseudo-posteriors, \texttt{fit\_dp\_lbbnn()}, and composite propensity losses (\texttt{STACK}, \texttt{LINK1/2}, \texttt{MIP}, \texttt{PSEUDO}) directly inside core \texttt{LBBNN} (v0.2.0).
  \item \textbf{Pros}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \scriptsize
    \item Zero cross-package dependency friction; direct access to internal R6 \texttt{lbbnn\_net} and LibTorch C++ closures.
    \item Broad visibility to the entire \texttt{LBBNN} user base.
  \end{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Cons}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \scriptsize
    \item Expands the scope and vignette footprint of the core general-purpose BNN package.
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}

\begin{column}{0.50\textwidth}
\textbf{Option B: Dedicated Companion (\texttt{LBBNNsurvey})}
\footnotesize
\begin{itemize}
  \setlength{\itemsep}{2.5pt}
  \item \textbf{Modular Extension Package}: Keep core \texttt{LBBNN} focused on foundational sparse BNNs (hooks for custom weights/losses) and release \texttt{LBBNNsurvey} importing \texttt{LBBNN}.
  \item \textbf{Pros}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \scriptsize
    \item Tailored identity for official statistics agencies (BLS, Census, Statistics Norway, Eurostat).
    \item Room to expand survey-specific tooling (Fay–Herriot small area models, Fellegi–Sunter linkage bridges, complex multi-stage bootstrap replicates, two-head joint architectures) on an independent release cycle.
  \end{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Cons}:
  \begin{itemize}
    \scriptsize
    \item Requires maintaining two synchronized CRAN packages.
  \end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\normalsize
\end{column}
\end{columns}
